key_insight: To understand why language-model data attribution fails, evaluations need to disentangle the dataset properties being tested. This paper introduces the Controlled Attribution Benchmark (CATT) to support more diagnostic evaluation of fact tracing.
problem_solved: Existing evaluations change multiple dataset properties at once, making it difficult to pinpoint why a method fails to trace a model’s factual output back to training data.
method: Explore the design space of language-model data attribution, focusing on evaluation.
Introduce CATT, a controlled benchmark for tracing facts to training data.
Use controlled evaluation to investigate attribution failures; the provided abstract is truncated and does not specify the full setup or results.
impact: More diagnostic evaluations could help practitioners distinguish attribution-method weaknesses from dataset effects and choose more reliable approaches for tracing model outputs to training sources.
visual_elements: Tracing diagram: training documents → language model → factual answer, with attribution arrows pointing back to sources.
Side-by-side comparison: confounded evaluation versus controlled evaluation.
Dataset-property sliders illustrating how separating variables helps diagnose failures.
Benchmark workflow: controlled data → model fine-tuning → fact tracing → failure analysis.
paper_title: Elucidating the Design Space of LM Data Attribution
paper_authors: Steven Yu, Sheng-Yu Wang, Kimia Hamidieh, Antonio Torralba, David Bau
